title: Zero-FI Regular ADHM Data and Framed ASD Connections

items.title: Donaldson's ADHM matrix equations in the source convention
items.statement:
Let $V=\mathbb C^k$ and $W=\mathbb C^N$ with their standard Hermitian inner products. Write $\alpha_1,\alpha_2\in\operatorname{End}_{\mathbb C}(V)$, $P:W\to V$, and $Q:V\to W$. The Donaldson source convention for these four matrices is

$$[\alpha_1,\alpha_2]+PQ=0,\qquad [\alpha_1,\alpha_1^\dagger]+[\alpha_2,\alpha_2^\dagger]-PP^\dagger+Q^\dagger Q=0.$$

The second equality is an equality of Hermitian endomorphisms of $V$. It is an algebraic convention from the displayed source equations; it does not by itself assert the full-rank condition on the source's ADHM linear map or an identification with the run's raw moment maps.

items.title: Zero-FI regular ADHM and framed twistor data
items.statement:
Fix integers $N\geq2$ and $k\geq0$. Let $V=\mathbb C^k$ and $W=\mathbb C^N$ with their standard Hermitian inner products. A raw framed ADHM datum is $x=(B_1,B_2,I,J)$ with $B_i\in\operatorname{End}_{\mathbb C}(V)$, $I:W\to V$, and $J:V\to W$. Its complex and real moment expressions are

$$\mu_{\mathbb C}(x)=[B_1,B_2]+IJ,\qquad \mu_{\mathbb R}(x)=[B_1,B_1^\dagger]+[B_2,B_2^\dagger]+II^\dagger-J^\dagger J.$$

The datum is stable when the vectors $B_{i_1}\cdots B_{i_m}I(w)$, for $m\geq0$, $i_j\in\{1,2\}$, and $w\in W$, span $V$. It is costable when no nonzero subspace of $V$ is invariant under both $B_1,B_2$ and contained in $\ker J$. It is regular when it is both stable and costable. The group $GL(V)$ acts by $g\cdot x=(gB_1g^{-1},gB_2g^{-1},gI,Jg^{-1})$ and its unitary subgroup is $U(V)$. The regular zero-FI real quotient is the orbit set

$$\mathcal A^{\mathrm{reg}}_{k,N}=\{x:\mu_{\mathbb C}(x)=0,\ \mu_{\mathbb R}(x)=0,\ x\text{ stable and costable}\}/U(V).$$

Let $S^4=\mathbb H\mathbb P^1$ have the unit round metric and the orientation whose restriction to the stereographic coordinates $z_1=x^0+ix^1$, $z_2=x^2+ix^3$ on $\mathbb R^4=S^4\setminus\{\infty\}$ is $-dx^0\wedge dx^1\wedge dx^2\wedge dx^3$. For a smooth right principal $U(N)$-bundle $P\to S^4$, let $E=P\times_{U(N)}\mathbb C^N$ be its Hermitian associated vector bundle, let $A$ be a smooth unitary connection, and let $\Phi:E|_{\infty}\to\mathbb C^N$ be a unitary framing. Write $F_A$ for the anti-Hermitian curvature matrix and define

$$q_N(P,A)=-\frac{1}{8\pi^2}\int_{S^4}\operatorname{tr}_N(F_A\wedge F_A).$$

The anti-self-dual equation is $F_A^+=(F_A+*_gF_A)/2=0$. For integer $k\geq0$, the framed ASD sector $\mathcal M^{\mathrm{ASD}}_{k,N}$ is the set of such framed connections satisfying $F_A^+=0$ and $q_N(P,A)=-k$, modulo smooth unitary gauge transformations whose value at $\infty$ is the identity in the framing. This definition alone does not assert that every sector exists or that $q_N$ is integral; the exact $U(N)$ charge normalization is a separate lemma below.

Identify $\mathbb H^2$ with $\mathbb C^4$ using a fixed right quaternionic structure $j$ with $j^2=-1$. The twistor space is $Z=\mathbb C\mathbb P^3=\mathbb P_{\mathbb C}(\mathbb H^2)$, the projection $\pi:Z\to\mathbb H\mathbb P^1=S^4$ sends a complex line $\ell$ to the quaternionic line $\ell+j\ell$, and the antiholomorphic involution is $\sigma([v])=[jv]$. A real twistor line is a fibre $L_x=\pi^{-1}(x)\cong\mathbb C\mathbb P^1$; $\sigma$ restricts to the antipodal map on each such line.


For the spinor convention, use the standard spin structure on $S^4$ and $\operatorname{Spin}(4)\cong SU(2)_+\times SU(2)_-$. Let $S^+,S^-$ be the associated rank-two complex spinor bundles, so $T_{\mathbb C}S^4\cong S^+\otimes S^-$. The twistor fibre at $x$ is $\mathbb P(S_x^+)$, and the complex two-plane associated with $\ell\in\mathbb P(S_x^+)$ is $\ell\otimes S_x^-$. Use the Levi-Civita connection of the round metric for the horizontal distribution of $\pi$; the horizontal $(0,1)$ subspace at $[\ell]\in L_x$ projects to this complex alpha-plane. The displayed orientation is the twistor orientation: the vertical complex orientation followed by the quotient orientation on $S^4$ agrees with the complex orientation on $Z$. It is chosen so the curvature component that vanishes on every such plane is precisely $F^+=(F+*_gF)/2$. In spinor components, $F_{AB}=F_{(AB)}$ denotes the symmetric spinor corresponding to $F^+$ under $\Lambda^2_+T_x^*S^4\otimes\mathbb C\cong\operatorname{Sym}^2(S_x^+)^*$; restriction to the plane is $F_{AB}\pi^A\pi^B$, which vanishes for every $[\pi]\in\mathbb P(S_x^+)$ exactly when $F^+=0$.

A linear monad on $Z$ is a complex of holomorphic bundles

$$\mathcal O_Z(-1)\otimes U\xrightarrow{a}\mathcal O_Z\otimes K\xrightarrow{b}\mathcal O_Z(1)\otimes U',$$

where $U,U',K$ are finite-dimensional complex vector spaces, $b\circ a=0$, $a$ is injective as a sheaf map, $b$ is surjective, and the cohomology sheaf $\ker b/\operatorname{im}a$ is locally free. It is framed when that cohomology has a specified unitary trivialization on $L_\infty$. For a holomorphic bundle $\mathcal E$ on $Z$, a positive Hermitian Ward reality datum consists of an isomorphism between its dual and its conjugate pullback by $\sigma$, with the Hermitian symmetry condition under $\sigma$, and positive Hermitian forms on $H^0(L_x,\mathcal E|_{L_x})$ varying smoothly with $x$. Each restriction $\mathcal E|_{L_x}$ is required to be holomorphically and unitarily trivial. Here the conjugate pullback uses the conjugate complex structure on the pulled-back fibres, so it is holomorphic; the symmetry condition means that the induced pairing at $\sigma z$ is the Hermitian adjoint of the pairing at $z$. A framed Ward bundle includes a unitary framing of $\mathcal E|_{L_\infty}$.

The compact torus $T=(S^1)^2\times(S^1)^N$ acts on $\mathbb R^4\cong\mathbb C^2$ by $(z_1,z_2)\mapsto(t_1z_1,t_2z_2)$ and on $W$ by $h=\operatorname{diag}(e_1^{-1},\ldots,e_N^{-1})$. Its raw ADHM action is

$$ (t_1,t_2,h)\cdot(B_1,B_2,I,J)=(t_1B_1,t_2B_2,Ih^{-1},t_1t_2hJ). $$

On the framed ASD sector, the same torus acts by inverse pullback under the indicated rotation of $S^4$ and by postcomposition of the framing with $h$. On $Z$, the rotations act by the projective spin lift to $\mathbb P(S^+)$; the central sign in the spin double cover acts trivially after projectivization, and the induced action commutes with $\sigma$. The framing torus acts on the framed monad cohomology by the same diagonal representation.

items.title: Entrywise conjugation does not match the raw ADHM real moment map
items.statement:
Let $(\alpha_1,\alpha_2,P,Q)$ obey the source equations stated in the following references section. Under the proposed substitution

$$B_i=\overline{\alpha_i},\qquad I=\overline P,\qquad J=\overline Q,$$

the raw complex moment map vanishes, but the raw real moment map is

$$\mu_{\mathbb R}=\overline C+\overline X-\overline Y,$$

where $C=[\alpha_1,\alpha_1^\dagger]+[\alpha_2,\alpha_2^\dagger]$, $X=PP^\dagger$, and $Y=Q^\dagger Q$. The conjugated source real equation gives $\overline C-\overline X+\overline Y=0$, so on source solutions the proposed raw real moment map equals $2\overline C$; the source equations alone therefore do not establish its vanishing. This failure occurs for the explicit $k=N=2$ source solution in the proof below.

items.title: Determinant flatness and charge normalization for framed U(N) ASD data
items.statement:
Assume full Axiom of Choice. Let $E\to S^4$ be a smooth Hermitian rank-$N$ vector bundle with $N\geq2$, a smooth unitary connection $A$, and a unitary framing at $\infty$. Give $S^4$ the round metric and the orientation specified in the definition of the framed ASD sector, and assume $F_A^+=0$. Then the induced determinant-line connection on $\det E=\Lambda^N E$ is flat. Its framing at $\infty$ determines a unique global unit parallel section, so the framed unitary bundle reduces to a framed $SU(N)$ bundle. With $q_N=-(8\pi^2)^{-1}\int_{S^4}\operatorname{tr}_N(F_A\wedge F_A)$ and the determinant Chern-form convention $c(A)=\det(I-F_A/(2\pi i))$, one has

$$q_N(E,A)=-\langle c_2(E),[S^4]\rangle\in-\mathbb Z_{\geq0}.$$

Thus $k=-q_N=\langle c_2(E),[S^4]\rangle$ is a nonnegative integer, with the sign corresponding to the anti-self-dual equation $F_A^+=0$.

items.title: Smooth framed bundle of sections over real twistor lines
items.statement:
Assume full AC and DC. Let $Z=\mathbb C\mathbb P^3$, let $G=\operatorname{Gr}(2,4)$ be the complex Grassmannian of projective lines in $Z$, and let $p:\mathscr L\to G$ be the universal line family with evaluation map $e:\mathscr L\to Z$. Let $\mathcal E\to Z$ be a holomorphic rank-$N$ bundle, $N\geq2$, with a positive Hermitian real structure and a unitary framing on the twistor line at $\infty$. Assume its restriction to every real twistor line $L_x$ is holomorphically and unitarily trivial. Assume also that, for every point $[L_x]\in G$ corresponding to a real twistor line, the cohomology-and-base-change map

$$\varphi^0_{[L_x]}:(p_*e^*\mathcal E)([L_x])\longrightarrow H^0(L_x,\mathcal E|_{L_x})$$

is surjective. Then $(p_*e^*\mathcal E)|_{S^4}$ is a smooth Hermitian rank-$N$ vector bundle, its fibre at $x$ is $H^0(L_x,\mathcal E|_{L_x})$, and the evaluation morphism identifies its pullback to the real incidence family with $e^*\mathcal E$. More precisely, for each line where the degree-zero base-change map is surjective, there is a complex-open neighbourhood in $G$ on whose entire universal-line family the evaluation morphism is an isomorphism. The framing on $L_\infty$ induces a unitary framing of this bundle at $\infty$.

items.title: Conditional framed Penrose–Ward correspondence on the round four-sphere
items.statement:
Assume full AC and the following two analytic/algebraic inputs: every smooth complex vector bundle on the complex three-manifold $Z=\mathbb CP^3$ with a smooth operator $\bar\partial_{\mathcal E}$ satisfying the Leibniz rule and $\bar\partial_{\mathcal E}^2=0$ has local frames in which that operator is the standard Dolbeault operator; and analytification on $\mathbb P^3_{\mathbb C}$ is an exact tensor-compatible equivalence for the bundles, morphisms, restrictions and projective-family base-change maps used below. These are conditional inputs, not conclusions of this theorem.

For $N\geq2$, let $\mathcal M^{\mathrm{ASD}}_{k,N}$ be the framed unitary ASD sector on the round oriented $S^4$ defined above. On the Ward side take a holomorphic rank-$N$ bundle $\mathcal E$ on $Z$, a positive Hermitian Ward reality datum, and a unitary framing on $L_\infty$. Require $\mathcal E|_{L_x}\cong\mathcal O_{L_x}^{\oplus N}$ for every real twistor line, require the degree-zero family base-change map to be surjective at every such line, and require $c_2(\mathcal E)=kH^2$, where $H=c_1(\mathcal O_Z(1))$. Then $\widehat E_x=H^0(L_x,\mathcal E|_{L_x})$ forms a smooth rank-$N$ Hermitian bundle on $S^4$. For each section of $\widehat E_x$, extend it holomorphically and uniquely to the first infinitesimal neighbourhood of $L_x$ and differentiate this extension in the family of lines; this defines the Ward connection $\widehat\nabla$. Include in the positive Hermitian Ward data the requirement that its specified positive Hermitian form on $\widehat E$ is smooth and is preserved by $\widehat\nabla$.

Under these hypotheses, the Ward construction gives a bijection between based unitary gauge classes in $\mathcal M^{\mathrm{ASD}}_{k,N}$ and isomorphism classes of the specified framed Ward bundles. The reconstructed Ward connection satisfies $F^+=0$ and $q_N=-k$. The inverse sends a framed ASD connection to the holomorphic structure on $\pi^*E$ whose vertical part is the standard Dolbeault operator and whose horizontal $(0,1)$ part is the connection on the planes $\ell\otimes S_x^-$. Both maps preserve the framing, Hermitian form, charge, and compact torus action. Reducible bundles and flat summands are included; no irreducibility assumption is imposed.

items.title: Chern character and charge of the normalized twistor monad
items.statement:
Let $\pi:Z=\mathbb CP^3\to S^4$ be the oriented twistor fibration with the conventions stated in the following references section, let $H=c_1(\mathcal O_Z(1))$, and let $E\to S^4$ be a framed unitary ASD rank-$N$ bundle whose Ward bundle is $\mathcal E=\pi^*E$ as a smooth bundle. Suppose $\mathcal E$ is the cohomology of a linear monad

$$\mathcal O_Z(-1)^{\oplus k}\longrightarrow\mathcal O_Z^{\oplus(2k+N)}\longrightarrow\mathcal O_Z(1)^{\oplus k}.$$

Then $\operatorname{ch}(\mathcal E)=N-kH^2$, $c_1(\mathcal E)=0$, and $c_2(\mathcal E)=kH^2$. For the twistor orientation specified in the Definition, if $u\in H^4(S^4;\mathbb Z)$ satisfies $\langle u,[S^4]\rangle=1$, then $\pi^*u=H^2$. Consequently

$$k=\langle c_2(E),[S^4]\rangle=-q_N(E,A).$$

items.title: Conditional Penrose vanishing from positive scalar curvature
items.statement:
Let $A$ be a smooth framed anti-self-dual unitary connection on the specified round oriented $S^4$, and let $\mathcal E$ be its holomorphic Ward bundle on $Z=\mathbb C\mathbb P^3$. Suppose the following conditional Penrose-transform input is supplied for both $\mathcal E$ and its dual $\mathcal E^\vee$: there are injective linear maps

$$\mathcal P_{\mathcal E}:H^1(Z,\mathcal E(-2))\longrightarrow\{s\in\Gamma(E):(\nabla_A^*\nabla_A+R/8)s=0\},$$

and the analogous map for $\mathcal E^\vee$, where $R>0$ is the scalar curvature of the round metric and the target connection is the induced unitary connection. Then

$$H^1(Z,\mathcal E(-2))=H^1(Z,\mathcal E^\vee(-2))=0.$$

This is a conditional vanishing result; it does not assert or prove the Penrose-transform input.

items.title: Conditional twistor vanishing and normalized monad reconstruction
items.statement:
Let $A$ be a framed unitary ASD connection on the round oriented $S^4$, let $\mathcal E$ be its Ward bundle on $Z=\mathbb CP^3$, and let $k=-q_N(A)$. Assume the conditional Penrose-transform input stated in the next paragraph for both $\mathcal E$ and $\mathcal E^\vee$. Assume also the exact projective GAGA and line-family base-change inputs needed to regard $\mathcal E$ as an algebraic bundle, to make its restrictions trivial on a complex-open neighbourhood of at least one real twistor line, and to apply the diagonal resolution. Finally, use the Chern-character normalization $\operatorname{ch}(\mathcal E)=N-kH^2$ in $A^*(\mathbb CP^3)_\mathbb Q$, where $H=c_1(\mathcal O(1))$; this normalization is conditional on the twistor pullback class convention matching the framed charge.

Under these inputs,

$$H^1(Z,\mathcal E(-2))=H^1(Z,\mathcal E^\vee(-2))=0.$$

There is a canonical Beilinson three-term monad

$$\mathcal O_Z(-1)\otimes U\longrightarrow\mathcal O_Z\otimes K\longrightarrow\mathcal O_Z(1)\otimes U',$$

whose middle cohomology is $\mathcal E$ and whose terms are

$$U=H^2(Z,\mathcal E(-3)),\qquad K=H^2(Z,\mathcal E\otimes\Omega_Z^2),\qquad U'=H^2(Z,\mathcal E\otimes\Omega_Z^1(-1)),$$

with $\dim U=\dim U'=k$ and $\dim K=2k+N$. The construction is natural in framed bundle isomorphisms and unique up to changes of bases in $U,K,U'$. If the ASD connection has a parallel subbundle, it splits orthogonally as a trivial flat summand and a summand with no nonzero parallel sections; the monad construction is additive across this splitting and uses no hypothesis $H^0(Z,\mathcal E)=0$.

items.title: Real monad normalization, regularity, framing and charge
items.statement:
Let $N\geq2$, $k\geq0$, and let a framed real Ward bundle on $Z=\mathbb CP^3$ have the normalized linear monad with vector-space dimensions $k,2k+N,k$. Then the real monad is equivalent to a raw datum $(B_1,B_2,I,J)$ on $V=\mathbb C^k$, $W=\mathbb C^N$ in exactly the convention

$$\mu_{\mathbb C}=[B_1,B_2]+IJ=0,\qquad \mu_{\mathbb R}=[B_1,B_1^\dagger]+[B_2,B_2^\dagger]+II^\dagger-J^\dagger J=0.$$

The tuple is regular exactly when the associated quaternionic construction is pointwise nondegenerate. Its kernel projection connection extends over $\infty$, has the specified framing, and equals the Ward connection. Changes of normalized monad bases induce exactly the $U(k)$ action on raw data, and inverse matrix extraction recovers the same $U(k)$ orbit. The resulting charge is $k=-q_N=\langle c_2(E),[S^4]\rangle$. A complete proof of the real monad-to-quaternionic block interface is still outstanding; the entrywise conjugation candidate is refuted by the calculation below and is not used as that proof.

items.title: Conditional zero-FI regular ADHM and framed ASD correspondence
items.statement:
Let $N\geq2$, $k\geq0$, and let $\mathcal M^{\mathrm{ADHM,reg}}_{k,N}$ be the quotient by $U(k)$ of the raw data satisfying both zero moment equations and stable-and-costable regularity in the conventions stated in the following references section. Let $\mathcal M^{\mathrm{ASD}}_{k,N}$ be the framed unitary ASD sector on the round oriented $S^4$ with $q_N=-k$ in those same conventions. Conditional on the real monad normalization and Ward inputs stated below, the construction gives a $T=(S^1)^2\times(S^1)^N$-equivariant bijection

$$\mathcal M^{\mathrm{ADHM,reg}}_{k,N}\;\longleftrightarrow\;\mathcal M^{\mathrm{ASD}}_{k,N}.$$

The zero-FI real quotient is also diffeomorphic to the stable-and-costable complex $GL(k)$ quotient. Under the stated projective GAGA and family base-change hypotheses, the corresponding framed sheaves on $\mathbb P^2$ are exactly the locally free locus among the framed torsion-free sheaves with rank $N$ and Hilbert polynomial $N\binom{m+2}{2}-k$. The positive-FI stable quotient includes non-locally-free sheaves and is not identified with the ordinary framed ASD moduli. Under the same family and normal-form hypotheses, the correspondence is compatible with first-order framed deformations and their tangent spaces.

title: Zero-FI Regular ADHM Data and Framed ASD Connections — Examples

items.title: The zero-charge regular datum and framed flat ASD sector
items.statement: For every $N\geq2$, the $k=0$ regular zero-FI ADHM quotient consists of the unique empty datum, and the framed ASD sector with $q_N=0$ consists of the framed flat connection on the trivial rank-$N$ bundle; the framing removes its based-gauge stabilizer.

items.title: A positive-FI point with a non-locally-free framed sheaf
items.statement:
Take $N=k=1$ and $\zeta>0$. The datum $B_1=B_2=0$, $I=\sqrt\zeta$, $J=0$ is a stable positive-FI solution but is not costable and does not lie in the zero-FI regular locus. Its stable complex orbit has the framed $\mathbb P^2$ monad

$$\mathcal O(-1)\xrightarrow{(-z_1,-z_2,0)^T}\mathcal O^{\oplus3}\xrightarrow{(z_2,-z_1,z_0)}\mathcal O(1),$$

whose middle cohomology is the ideal sheaf of $p=[1:0:0]$; it is torsion-free and not locally free at $p$. Thus this positive-FI point lies on the non-locally-free boundary excluded from the ordinary zero-FI framed ASD correspondence.
